paper_title: Achieving Anonymity via Weak Lower Bound Constraints for k-Median and k-Means
classifications: Theory of computation → Facility location and clustering
statement: Given a β ≥ 21 and a γ-approximate solution to generalized k-median with 2-weak lower 2 αβ α β bounds (C, a), we can compute a (β, γ max{ 1−β + 1, 1−β })-bicriteria solution in the following way. Let C = {c1 , . . . , ck′ } for some k ′ ≤ k. We process the centers in order c1 , . . . , ck′ and decide if they are open or closed. We say that ci is smaller than cj if i < j. If we decide that a center c is open we directly assign at least ⌈βB(c)⌉ points to c. In the beginning all points are unassigned. Consider center ci . Let Ai be the set of all points assigned to ci under a. We know that |Ai | ≥ B(ci ). If at least ⌈βB(ci )⌉ points in Ai are not assigned so far, ci remains open and all currently unassigned points from Ai are assigned to ci (Figure 4). If less than ⌈βB(ci )⌉ points from Ai are unassigned, the center is closed. Let C ′ denote the centers from {c1 , . . . , ci−1 } which are open and Bi the set of unassigned points from Ai which are not connected to any center larger than ci under a. To guarantee that all points are assigned at the end, we have to care about points in Bi . By assumption there are at most ⌊βB(ci )⌋ such points. We simply assign a point p ∈ Bi to the nearest center arg minc∈C ′ d(c, p) in C ′ .
